# Tharun Project — Automated Comparative Analysis of Code Generated by a Beginner, an LLM, and an Expert

**Author:** Tharun · **Institution:** University of Roehampton

An offline re-runnable benchmark analysis tool that compares Python solutions
from three *sources* — **beginner**, **LLM**, and **expert** — across a curated
benchmark of programming tasks. It measures static-analysis quality (complexity,
maintainability, size, Halstead volume, style, security), runs each solution
against functional tests, performs non-parametric statistics, draws
black-and-white-friendly figures, and writes a full report — all offline, with no
API keys and no servers.

> ### Honest framing — please read
> The dataset is a **curated, representative benchmark** of **30 tasks** (10 per
> tier). For every task the **beginner** and **expert** solutions are single
> authored reference implementations typifying each source; the **LLM** solutions
> are **labelled as model-generated** (the archive identifies Claude Opus 4.8; provider receipts are not supplied), sampled 5 times per task
> under a fixed prompt (see [`dataset/LLM_PROVENANCE.md`](dataset/LLM_PROVENANCE.md)).
> **No code was scraped from real students, assistants, or professionals.** All
> results characterise *this benchmark only* and must not be generalised to any
> wider population. It is intended — and deliberately left unfixed — that beginner
> solutions fail some edge-case tests on the harder tasks; **that monotonic
> decline is the experimental signal — it shows the pipeline can detect such
> differences, not that real beginners fail at these rates.**

---

## What it produces

| Location | Contents |
|---|---|
| `outputs/metrics.csv`, `outputs/metrics.json` | One row per (task × source × sample) with every metric + functional result |
| `outputs/stats.json`, `outputs/stats.md` | Full statistical analysis (machine- and human-readable) |
| `figures/*.png` | Box plots, pass-rate-by-difficulty bars, overall radar chart |
| `report/report.md`, `report/report.html`, `report/report.docx` | The final report (numbers traced to `outputs/`) |
| `report/dashboard.html` | Self-contained interactive **web dashboard** (offline, no server needed) |
| `screenshots/code/`, `screenshots/gui/` | Code screenshots and dashboard/output screenshots (auto-captured) |
| `evidence/*` | Raw, verbatim output of every external tool call + `run.log` |

## Requirements

- Python 3.10+ (developed and verified on 3.13).
- The packages in `requirements.txt` (radon, pylint, bandit, pytest, pandas,
  numpy, scipy, matplotlib, jinja2, markdown, tabulate, python-docx). No other
  third-party packages are used anywhere.

## Install

```bash
cd tharun-project        # the project root (this directory)
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Or simply: `make setup`.

## Run (one command)

```bash
python run_analysis.py
```

That runs the entire pipeline in order: **validate dataset → functional
correctness → static metrics → statistics → figures → report**, then prints a
`RESULTS SUMMARY`. Useful flags:

```bash
python run_analysis.py --verbose            # DEBUG console logging
python run_analysis.py --tier advanced      # only one difficulty tier
python run_analysis.py --skip-figures       # skip figure generation
python run_analysis.py --skip-report        # skip report generation
```

Run the framework's own unit tests (these must pass):

```bash
pytest tests/
```

### Windows without `make`

Every `make` target maps to a plain command: `make setup` → the venv + pip
commands above; `make run` → `python run_analysis.py`; `make test` →
`pytest tests/`; `make report` → `python -c "from src import report; report.build_report()"`.

## How the three sources differ (by design)

- **beginner** — works on the common cases but: short/poor names, little
  decomposition (one long function), higher complexity and nesting, no type hints,
  weak/absent docstrings, **misses some edge tests on the harder tasks**, and
  occasionally uses a sloppy-but-safe pattern (e.g. `assert` for validation or a
  bare `try/except: pass`) that security scanners flag.
- **expert** — idiomatic, decomposed, fully type-hinted and documented, low
  complexity, handles every edge case, clean, no security flags.
- **llm** — **model-labelled archived output** (reported as Claude Opus 4.8), 5 archived
  samples per task: correct and readable but typically verbose and defensive
  (extra comments, redundant checks, slightly higher Halstead volume); passes
  most/all tests. The five labelled samples vary, so a descriptive `pass@k` (k>1) can be calculated and
  the LLM arm shows within-source variance. See `dataset/LLM_PROVENANCE.md`.

## Project layout

```
tharun-project/
  run_analysis.py        # single entry point (argparse CLI)
  config.py              # paths, seed, metric definitions, the 7 references
  pyproject.toml         # project metadata + pytest/pylint/bandit config
  LICENSE                # MIT
  src/                   # correctness, metrics, statistics, visualize, report,

  dataset/tasks/<id>/    # meta.json, solutions/{beginner,expert}.py +
                         #   solutions/llm/sample_1..5.py (model-labelled; provider logs not supplied),
                         #   solutions/llm_curated_reference.py, tests/
  dataset/LLM_PROVENANCE.md   # model, prompt, date for the LLM samples
  outputs/ figures/ report/ evidence/    # deliverables (tracked)
  screenshots/code/ screenshots/gui/     # code & dashboard screenshots
  tools/capture_screenshots.py           # headless-Chromium screenshotter
  docs/                  # SCREENSHOT_GUIDE.md, SONARQUBE.md (optional)
  sonar/                 # optional SonarQube template (not required to run)
  tests/test_pipeline.py # framework unit tests (must pass)
  .github/workflows/ci.yml   # CI: tests + pylint + bandit + pipeline smoke
```

## Engineering quality (CI, linting, security)

The framework holds itself to the same bar it measures:

- **The tool dogfoods itself.** `pylint src/ run_analysis.py config.py` scores
  **10.00/10**, and `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r src/ run_analysis.py config.py` reports **zero**
  findings. (The `dataset/` solutions are deliberately imperfect study subjects
  and are excluded from these scans.)
- **Continuous integration.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the unit tests,
  the pylint gate (`--fail-under=10`), the bandit scan, and a full end-to-end
  pipeline smoke test on Python 3.10–3.13, then uploads the artifacts.
- **Web server hardened.** The optional dashboard server binds to **loopback
  only** (`127.0.0.1`) and the pipeline-re-run endpoint is **disabled by
  default** (opt in with `--enable-rerun`). The dashboard template renders with
  Jinja2 autoescaping on; the only raw-HTML fields are pre-escaped and the
  embedded JSON is escaped so it cannot break out of its `<script>` block.
- **Valid, deterministic outputs.** `outputs/*.json` are strictly valid JSON
  (degenerate statistics collapse to `null`, never `NaN`), and the analysis is
  byte-for-byte reproducible (see below).
- **Packaging.** `pyproject.toml` carries the project metadata, pins the runtime
  dependencies, and configures pytest/pylint/bandit. `pip install .` works.

Run the same gates locally:

```bash
pytest tests/                                       # unit tests
pylint src/ run_analysis.py config.py               # 10.00/10
bandit -c pyproject.toml -r src/ run_analysis.py config.py   # 0 findings
```

## Determinism

All random seeds are fixed to 42, matplotlib uses the `Agg` backend, and metrics
come from each tool's JSON CLI. The same inputs produce the same outputs every
run. (Only the *timestamp* in the report appendix varies; no analytical number
depends on it.)

## Metrics & methods at a glance

- **radon** → cyclomatic complexity (McCabe), maintainability index, raw size
  (LOC/LLOC/SLOC/comments), Halstead volume.
- **pylint** → style score (/10) and issue count.
- **bandit** → security findings by severity.
- **pytest** → functional correctness in separate temporary subprocesses (not a security sandbox); the `pass@k`
  estimator (Chen et al. 2021) is computable descriptively for the LLM-labelled arm (5 samples per task, so
  pass@1 and pass@5 are both reported); the single-sample human arms report pass@1.
- **scipy** → Shapiro-Wilk (diagnostic), Friedman matched-task omnibus, paired Wilcoxon with within-metric
  Bonferroni adjustments, paired rank-biserial effect size, Cochran Q and
  exact McNemar for one preselected LLM sample per task.

The static-metric tests (and the medians shown in the report and figures) use
**one observation per (task, source)** — each source's per-task median across its
samples — so the 5-sample LLM arm is weighted equally with the single-sample human
arms (a balanced 30 vs 30 vs 30) instead of 5×. The per-sample data feed only the
`pass@k` estimator and the per-sample pass rate; every raw sample remains in
`outputs/metrics.csv` and the report appendix.

## Web dashboard (interactive GUI)

The pipeline also builds **`report/dashboard.html`** — a single self-contained
page (monochrome, matching the project's B/W style) with tabs for Overview,
Metrics Explorer (sortable/filterable table), Statistics, Figures, a **Code
Browser** (all 30 tasks × 3 sources, syntax-highlighted, with each solution's
metrics; the LLM arm shows a representative sample of the 5), and Findings. Every
figure and number is embedded, so it opens offline with no server:

```bash
xdg-open report/dashboard.html        # just open the file — works on file://
```

Prefer a live server (with an optional in-browser "re-run" button)? It uses only
the Python standard library:

```bash
python -m src.webapp serve            # http://localhost:8000  (make webapp)
```

### Screenshots (split into two folders)

`screenshots/` holds ready-made captures, separated by kind:

- **`screenshots/code/`** — source-code screenshots: the beginner/llm/expert
  solutions side by side for representative tasks (`two_sum.png`, `dijkstra.png`, …).
- **`screenshots/gui/`** — dashboard output views (`01_overview.png`,
  `02_metrics.png`, `03_statistics.png`, `04_figures.png`, `05_code_browser.png`,
  `06_findings.png`).

See `screenshots/README.md` for the full index. Regenerate any time with headless
Chromium:

```bash
python tools/capture_screenshots.py            # both folders   (make screenshots)
python tools/capture_screenshots.py --only code   # just code shots
python tools/capture_screenshots.py --only gui    # just GUI shots
```

## Optional extensions (off by default, never required)

- **Regenerate the LLM solutions from a live API** — the committed LLM samples are
  labelled as model output (not independently authenticated) (see `dataset/LLM_PROVENANCE.md`).
  `src/regenerate_llm.py` can refresh them from a live API, but only does anything
  when the `LLM_API_KEY` environment variable is set; the core pipeline never calls
  it and works fully offline. See the file's docstring.
- **SonarQube** — `sonar/sonar-project.properties` + **[docs/SONARQUBE.md](docs/SONARQUBE.md)**
  describe an optional `sonar-scanner` workflow. The core pipeline uses
  radon/pylint/bandit and **never** needs a SonarQube server.

## Troubleshooting

**All static metrics come back `N/A`.** The pipeline resolves `radon`, `pylint`
and `bandit` from the directory of the running interpreter (`src/metrics.py`).
If the packages are installed somewhere other than next to the interpreter being
used — for example a system-wide `pip install` rather than a virtual environment
— those executables are not found, the lookup fails quietly, and every static
metric is recorded as missing while the run still exits 0. Run the pipeline from
the virtual environment created in **Install** above (`.venv/bin/python
run_analysis.py`), or activate it first.

**`pytest tests/` fails to collect.** Confirm every dependency in
`requirements.txt` is installed in the environment being used; the test module
imports the full pipeline.

**Verifying a clean run.** `bash verify.sh` performs a fresh virtual-environment
install, records tool versions, runs the framework tests and quality gates,
executes the full pipeline and checks the output counts, writing everything to a
timestamped log.

## Revision dated 2026-10-15 — important evidence limitations

The corrected `outputs/stats.json` and `outputs/stats.md` use a matched-task design.
Original `outputs/metrics.csv` and raw evidence are retained **unchanged**.
Statistical results come from the archived metrics, not a newly run end-to-end
analysis. `report/` content should be treated as regenerated from these archived
metrics only. The original LLM generation had access to visible test files;
reported original pass@k is **not a blind generalisation estimate**.

Supplementary tests under `supplementary/` were authored **after** model
generation and checked against specifications. They have not been blind-selected
by independent researchers. Results are a sensitivity study; they do not turn
the original test-visible benchmark into a prospective controlled study.

For security, copying a solution into a temporary directory and running it in
a subprocess is process separation, **not** a hostile-code sandbox. Do not run
untrusted third-party code on a privileged production host. A network-disabled,
read-only, resource-limited container or VM is required for untrusted inputs.

The original Git history, model provider response IDs, generation-time logs,
a signed declaration and an actual screencast are not contained in this package.
These must be supplied by the student if available, not manufactured.

## Strict preflight and process limits (2026-10-15 revision)

`run_analysis.py` now refuses to start if Radon, Pylint or Bandit are missing.
Do not interpret `N/A` metrics as ordinary scores. The runner disables unrelated
Pytest auto-loaded plugins and applies best-effort POSIX CPU, address-space and
file-size limits to subprocesses; this is **not a security sandbox** and does
not block network activity or filesystem access. Use Docker/VM isolation before
introducing untrusted code. A successful complete pipeline rerun on the target
machine remains necessary before academic sign-off.


## 2026-10-15 research-integrity audit addendum

- `python tools/audit_baselines.py` produces inspectable structural metrics and hashes for the 60 constructed reference files (`verification/`). This is not a blind human review. In this dataset, all 30 expert references and no beginner references have entry-point docstrings and return annotations; the labels were intentionally engineered, creating design-induced separation.
- The baseline/reviewer protocol in `verification/INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_FORM.md` is **blank** pending a real assessor. Do not claim its completion.
- `verification/preflight.log` documents why a fresh full pipeline cannot be certified in the current review environment; the original 210-row archived metrics are preserved.
- Current framework tests excluding the external static-tool integration test pass; this does not certify the excluded test or the complete GitHub workflow.
- Original generation-visible tests and retrospective supplementary cases must not be called independently blinded validation. More robust research would require a new prospectively separated generation/evaluation protocol with independently assessed task specifications and actual human cohorts (with approval).

## Current evidence status and external validation preparation

The archive has an independent index/inventory audit (`python tools/audit_repro_evidence.py`): 30 task folders, 210 unique source records and all 1,680 expected per-sample raw evidence files **present**. This checks completeness, not correctness of raw analyzer values. The full 2026-10-15/16 review environment could not install Radon, Pylint or Bandit, so a **fresh 210-row static re-extraction is not claimed**. A fail-fast `bash verify.sh` is provided for an appropriately isolated connected computer; save its actual `.status` and `.log` files before claiming reproduction.

There are two prepared (not performed) validation resources: `verification/independent_review_preparation/REVIEWER_PACKET/` hides constructed source labels for a future reviewer; `verification/external_test_author_packet.zip` gives specifications but no candidate files or previous tests to a future external test writer. Neither resource constitutes completed human research or prospectively blinded testing. Prospective model-generation experiments and collection of novice/expert code require authentic new participants/model calls, suitable permissions and genuine contemporaneous records.

The student must separately supply original development/supervision evidence (if it exists), their own signature and date, an accessible screencast, and reference verification; no such evidence has been fabricated.
